thread:
Samuel (AcmeDev): hey team, after the 2026-03-14 rollout our codegen outputs for Go and Python are producing compilation errors. This started ~2am UTC when our CI first ran. Previously identical prompts compiled fine.
Maya (CSE): thanks Samuel — can you paste one failing example + the exact API payload you used? we'll triage. :eyes: cc @Lina and @Arjun
Samuel (AcmeDev): here's a minimal repro. request to /v1/generate (JS SDK) — produces a function missing imports and wrong signature.
```
const res = await redwood.generate({
  model: "codegen-stable-2026-03-14",
  input: "Write a Go function that parses a JSON body into struct User { ID int; Name string } and returns 400 on error",
  temperature: 0.0,
  max_tokens: 300
})
console.log(res.output)
```
The output starts with `func ParseUser(body io.Reader) User {` (no error return), and it omits `import ("encoding/json" "io" "net/http")` — then our build fails with undefined `json` and missing error handling.
Maya (CSE): ouch. can you also paste the compile error from CI?
Samuel (AcmeDev): sure — Go build failure snippet: `./handler.go:42:11: undefined: json` and `handler.go:24:6: missing return at end of function`.
Lina (eng): thanks — initial question: what exact model id/version did you previously use that worked? any `model_version` pinned?
Samuel (AcmeDev): we were on `codegen-stable-2026-03-07` and switched to the 03-14 rollout automatically via hosted default. We didn't pin.
Arjun (product): tagging rollout notes: 03-14 deploy included the tokenizer normalizer + a formatting postprocess (strip_leading_comments) aimed at removing license headers. Could be related.
Lina (eng): can we repro internally? @ops_oncall can you run the same payload with both model versions and attach diffs?
ops_oncall: running now. will post diff in ~5m.
support-bot: created support ticket rwin-4821; priority P1 per customer CI break.
(5m later)
ops_oncall: attached results: with 03-07 model the output includes `import (...)` and `func ParseUser(body io.Reader) (User, error) {` — with 03-14 it drops error return and imports. Diff looks like missing import block + altered function signature.
Lina (eng): that aligns with formatting postprocess bug hypothesis — strip_leading_comments may have been too aggressive and trimmed the import block when code didn't start with a comment. but imports shouldn't be removed. I'm going to reproduce locally with the backend binary + the exact codegen pipeline.
Maya (CSE): Samuel, quick question — are you sending `stream: true` or any `preserve_formatting` flag? and does setting temperature to 0.0 vs 0.2 change anything?
Samuel (AcmeDev): we use streaming in CI (to accumulate tokens) but we tried non-streaming earlier and still saw the regression. temp 0.0 and 0.2 both fail.
Lina (eng): repro steps I'm running (internal):
1) curl POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"codegen-stable-2026-03-14","input":"Write a Go function that parses a JSON body into struct User { ID int; Name string } and returns 400 on error","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":300}'
2) save output to file and run `gofmt` + `go vet`
I see the same missing import. digging into pipeline: tokenizer normalization, then prefix-safety, then postprocess formatters.
Arjun (product): there's a canary flag still alive for 03-14: rollout=% of traffic = 30%. we rolled to 100% last night per automation. we can revert to 03-07 or reduce rollout. thoughts?
Maya (CSE): Samuel, would you accept a temporary mitigation: pin your requests with `model: "codegen-stable-2026-03-07"` or add `preserve_formatting` (if available) while we investigate?
Samuel (AcmeDev): pinning is fine temporarily but we want a fix asap. CI is blocked on multiple PRs.
Lina (eng): found root cause: the new tokenizer normalizer collapses certain newline/comment patterns; the postprocesser that re-inserts imports relied on detecting `import (` pattern at token boundaries. Normalization changed token boundaries so the re-insertion step failed and removed import block when heuristics thought it was duplicate. creating patch to skip import-removal when language==go and imports detected.
Lina (eng): patch ready, running unit tests + internal staging. ETA deploy in ~2 hours if tests pass.
ops_oncall: I can roll back the rollout to 5% as a precaution; want me to do that now?
Arjun (product): yes please, rollback to 5% and mark as rollback_in_progress. communicate to infra that we should hold the full 100% until patch is in prod.
ops_oncall: rollback started. current rollout: 5%. logs showing traffic shift. :white_check_mark:
Maya (CSE): Samuel — we've reduced exposure and Lina is working on a patch. two options for you: pin to 03-07 or we can flip a tenant-level flag to pin you to previous model until patch deploys. which do you prefer?
Samuel (AcmeDev): tenant flag would be great so others can still get latest. please set it. also, is there a lambda or SDK-level workaround?
Maya (CSE): setting tenant flag now.
(10m)
Maya (CSE): done — tenant pinned to codegen-stable-2026-03-07 for AcmeDev. CI should pick that up in next run.
Samuel (AcmeDev): confirmed CI passed on next run. thanks.
Lina (eng): patch merged to main; rolling through staging. key change: skip import-removal postprocess for Go unless import block tokenized as whole. added unit test covering multiple comment/import patterns.
Arjun (product): scheduling a postmortem and adding an eval check in the release pipeline: run a compile-check for top-3 languages before bumping canary above 25%.
Maya (CSE): summarizing action items: 1) Tenant pin set for AcmeDev (done) 2) Rollback to 5% (done) 3) Eng patch merged and in staging (Lina) 4) Postmortem + release gate (Arjun) 5) Support ticket rwin-4821 will track release and customer communication.
Samuel (AcmeDev): appreciate the fast response. please keep me posted in this thread. :pray:
support-bot: rwin-4821 updated — status: monitoring; next update ETA 2h.
